translation_fidelity_review.summary: Fresh cross-model translation-fidelity audit (Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh, read-only, fresh thread). Codex independently read the Chinese source of truth (docs/tutorials/attention_tutorial.md), the English translation (docs/tutorials/attention_tutorial_en.md), and the rendered English HTML (docs/tutorials/attention_tutorial_en.html), then compared EN against ZH across all five fidelity axes: (a) numbers/formulas/code/tensor shapes, (b) citations (author/year/venue) and model names, (c) completeness (no dropped section/claim/caveat, no new hallucinated claim), (d) terminology consistency, and (e) HTML

post_ship_review.scope: 2026-07-12 full-collection re-sweep: Codex GPT-5.6-sol candidate pass + independent Claude Sonnet 5 adversarial verification (attempted to refute every candidate finding; only load-bearing ones kept)
post_ship_review.summary: 8 findings verified against the ZH source (4 CONFIRMED + 4 NEEDS_NUANCE, 0 REFUTED); EN edition mirrors the ZH fixes with natural (non-machine-translated) phrasing.
fixes: §1: 'Q/K/V share the same source, three projections' scoped explicitly to self-attention, with a cross-attention pointer to §4
§6.1: cumulative redundant compute over T generation steps without KV cache corrected O(t^2) -> O(T^3)
§6.1: 'KV cache cannot be used in training' softened — true for teacher-forced parallel SFT/pretraining, false for RLHF/GRPO on-policy rollout generation
§6.1: LLaMA-2-70B KV cache size relabeled GB -> GiB (1.25 GiB approx 1.34 GB; vanilla MHA 10 GiB approx 10.74 GB)
§6.2: GQA table 'used in' column qualified to LLaMA-2-70B only (7B/13B are still MHA)
§10 Q24: RoPE bullet restored the 'content vectors still determine the score' caveat already present in the §8 table

§A appendix rewritten to describe the actual code/mha.py (3 sanity checks: sanity_check/shape_check/causal_check; single self-attention MultiHeadAttention with fused qkv Linear and [N,N] mask; no SelfAttention/CrossAttention wrappers, no 4 mask shapes, no NaN guard) instead of fabricated 9-check output — chose to align appendix text to reality rather than add new code

§A appendix sanity-check transcript's exception type corrected ValueError -> AssertionError, matching mha.py's actual `assert embed_dim % num_heads == 0`; added a note that `assert` is stripped under python -O
post_ship_review.note: Re-rendered attention_tutorial_en.html and refreshed source_sha256 (this run); gated via tools/verify_reviews.py --mode strict --reproduce.

delta_reviews.scope: New §3.5 only (fused QKV: chunk / split / 5-D reshape+permute; GQA chunk(3) trap). No other content touched.
delta_reviews.process: Claims verified on a real PyTorch box before drafting (all three slicing forms torch.equal; GQA chunk(3) widths [43,43,42] failing later at view; chunk on width 5 -> [2,2,1]). Reviewer then re-derived all six claims and audited prose.
findings_fixed: Form 2 (split) as printed stopped at [B,N,D] — missing the same view+transpose the chunk form gets; added, re-verified verbatim.
'differ only in GEMM count' compared the wrong pair — the three slicing forms share one GEMM; 3-to-1 is fused vs §3.4's three Linears. Reworded.

GPT-2 c_attn orientation: it is a Conv1D with weight [D,3D], Q/K/V concatenated along the OUTPUT dim — 'stacked vertically' described the transposed nn.Linear layout. Corrected, with the transpose note.
'real code almost always fuses' overstated — scoped to self-attention, with HF LLaMA (separate q/k/v_proj) and cross-attention (cannot fuse) as counterexamples.
'far better' tensor-core utilisation softened to shape/backend-dependent.
'the only correct form under MQA/GQA' narrowed to the true rule: never equal-chunk(3) unequal widths; explicit-width split is the standard form.
